c: Youth Agitations & Paper Leaks
Dr. K. Radhakrishnan High-Level Committee (2024)
Ministry of Education
High-level panel formed to reform the National Testing Agency (NTA), overhaul exam security protocols, enhance digital paper transmission, and safeguard youth interests.
Communalism & National Integration
Justice Liberhan & Srikrishna Commissions
Ministry of Home Affairs
Inquiries into major communal riots/events; laid structural guidelines for police accountability, riot prevention, and impartial district administration.
Regionalisation & North East Conflicts
Justice B.P. Jeevan Reddy Committee (2005)
Ministry of Home Affairs
Recommended the repeal of AFSPA, 1958 and suggested inserting relevant protective clauses into the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act to mitigate regional alienation.
Centre-State Relations & Regionalism
Sarkaria Commission (1988) & Punchhi Commission (2010)
Ministry of Home Affairs
Addressed federal tensions, deployment of central armed forces, inter-state council revitalization, and objective criteria for invoking Article 356.
Scheduled Castes (SC) & Scheduled Tribes (ST)
State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024)

7-judge bench overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004); affirmed states have constitutional power under Arts. 15(4) & 16(4) to sub-classify SCs/STs using empirical data; recommended creamy layer identification.
Scheduled Castes (SC) & Scheduled Tribes (ST)
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
Upheld reservation in promotions for SC/STs subject to quantifiable data demonstrating backwardness, inadequate representation, and overall administrative efficiency (Art. 335).
Scheduled Castes (SC) & Scheduled Tribes (ST)
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018)
Removed the requirement to prove backwardness for SC/STs in promotions; extended the creamy layer principle to SC/ST promotions.
Scheduled Castes (SC) & Scheduled Tribes (ST)
Samatha v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1997)
Nullified mining leases to non-tribals in Schedule V areas; held that tribal land cannot be leased to private parties or corporations.
Scheduled Castes (SC) & Scheduled Tribes (ST)
Orissa Mining Corp. v. MoEF (Niyamgiri Case, 2013)
Affirmed statutory role of the Gram Sabha under FRA 2006 to safeguard religious and cultural rights of Dongria Kondh tribals.
Other Backward Classes (OBC)
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) (Mandal Case)
Upheld 27% quota for OBCs; introduced the creamy layer exclusion; fixed the 50% reservation ceiling; ruled out quotas in promotions.
Other Backward Classes (OBC)
Janki Prasad Parimoo v. State of J&K (1973)
Clarified that caste alone cannot be the sole determinant of backwardness under Article 15(4); must include social and educational indicators.
Economically Weaker Sections (EWS)
Janki Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)
Upheld the validity of the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act (10% EWS quota), ruling economic criteria alone can form a valid basis for classification.
Persons with Disabilities (PwD)
Rajive Raturi v. Union of India (2018)
Framed concrete directions for time-bound visual, auditory, and mobility accessibility in public transport and built infrastructure under the RPwD Act.
Persons with Disabilities (PwD)
Vikash Kumar v. UPSC (2021)
Scribe facility cannot be restricted only to persons with benchmark disabilities; recognized "reasonable accommodation" as an intrinsic component of equality.
Minorities
T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002)
Unit for determining religious and linguistic minority status under Article 30 is the State, not the entire nation.
Workplace Safety & Harassment
Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)
Laid down binding guidelines against sexual harassment at the workplace under Articles 14, 19, and 21; directly led to the POSH Act, 2013.
Marriage & Personal Law
Shayara Bano v. Union of India (2017)
Declared instant Talaq-e-Biddat (Triple Talaq) unconstitutional, arbitrary, and violative of Article 14.
Marriage & Personal Law
Danial Latifi v. Union of India (2001)
Upheld the Muslim Women Act, 1986; ruled that maintenance is not limited solely to the iddat period and must cover reasonable provision for the wife's entire life.
Marriage & Personal Law
Saroj Rani v. Sudarshan Kumar Chadha (1984)
Upheld the constitutional validity of Restitution of Conjugal Rights (RCR) under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act.
Gender Autonomy & Property
Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020)
Clarified Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005; daughters have coparcenary rights by birth regardless of whether the father was alive on the amendment date.
Gender Autonomy & Property
Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018)
Struck down Section 497 of IPC (Adultery) as archaic, patriarchal, and violative of Articles 14 and 21.
Gender Autonomy & Property
X v. Principal Secretary, H&FW, GNCTD (2022)
Ruled that all women, regardless of marital status, are entitled to safe and legal abortion up to 24 weeks under the MTP Act; included marital rape within medical termination rules.
Transgender & Queer Rights
NALSA v. Union of India (2014)
Recognized transgender individuals as the Third Gender; affirmed their fundamental right to self-identify their gender identity.
Transgender & Queer Rights
Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India (2018)
Decriminalized consensual same-sex adult relationships by reading down Section 377 of the IPC.
Child Protection & Labour
M.C. Mehta v. State of Tamil Nadu (1996)
Banned child labour in hazardous industries; mandated establishment of a Child Labour Rehabilitation-cum-Welfare Fund.
Child Protection & Labour
Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017)
Struck down the marital rape exception for minor wives under IPC Section 375; intercourse with a girl below 18 is statutory rape, regardless of marriage.
Child Protection & Labour
Bachpan Bachao Andolan v. Union of India (2011)
Issued guidelines against trafficking, child begging, and circus child labor; mandated human-rights oversight of all Child Care Institutions.
Communalism & Secularism
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)
Ruled that Secularism is a basic feature of the Constitution; state governments acting against secularism can be dismissed under Article 356.
Communalism & Secularism
Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen (2017)
Expanded Section 123(3) of RPA 1951; appeals to religion, race, caste, community, or language during election campaigns constitute a corrupt practice.
Caste Violence & Mob Lynching
Tehseen S. Poonawalla v. Union of India (2018)
Issued guidelines for preventive, corrective, and punitive measures to combat mob lynching and cow vigilantism.
Caste Violence & Mob Lynching
Shakti Vahini v. Union of India (2018)
Declared Khap Panchayat interferences and honor killings illegal; affirmed the right to choose a life partner as part of Article 21.
Youth Agitations & Public Protest
Amit Sahni v. Commissioner of Police (Shaheen Bagh, 2020)
Recognized the right to protest peacefully under Article 19, but held that public ways and spaces cannot be occupied indefinitely.
Youth Agitations & Public Protest
In Re: Destruction of Public and Private Properties (2009)
Held that leaders and organizers of agitations resulting in property destruction are subject to vicarious civil and criminal liability.
Special Marriage Act
January 1, 1955
Civil, secular marriage framework independent of religious rites.
Hindu Marriage Act
Codified conditions of Hindu marriage, divorce, and restitution of conjugal rights.
Hindu Succession Act
June 17, 1956 (Amended: Sept 9, 2005)
Property inheritance rights; 2005 amendment gave equal coparcenary rights to daughters by birth.
Dowry Prohibition Act
July 1, 1961
Strictly penalizes giving, taking, or demanding dowry.
Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act
April 1, 1972 (Amended: Sept 24, 2021)
Legalized abortion up to 24 weeks on specified therapeutic and vulnerable-group grounds.
Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act
January 1, 1996
Prohibits prenatal sex determination to stop female feticide.
Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA)
October 26, 2006
Civil remedies: protection orders, right to reside, and maintenance via Protection Officers.
Prohibition of Child Marriage Act (PCMA)
November 1, 2007
Replaced the 1929 Sarda Act; fixes minimum age at 18 (females) and 21 (males); child marriages are voidable.
Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act
December 9, 2013
Mandates Internal Complaints Committees (ICC) in workplaces with 10 or more employees.
Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act
September 19, 2018 (Retrospective effect; Royal Assent July 31, 2019)
Criminalizes instant Triple Talaq (Talaq-e-Biddat) with up to 3 years of imprisonment.
Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act
December 23, 1986 (Major Amendment: Sept 1, 2016)
Complete prohibition of employment of children below 14; restricts adolescent work in hazardous processes.
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights (CPCR) Act
February 15, 2006
Constituted NCPCR and SCPCRs as statutory bodies for child welfare monitoring.
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act
April 1, 2010
Enforces Article 21A (ages 6–14); mandates 25% quota in private unaided schools for disadvantaged groups.
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act
November 14, 2012 (Amended: August 16, 2019)
Gender-neutral law punishing child sexual abuse; 2019 amendment added capital punishment for aggravated penetrative assault.
Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection of Children) Act
January 15, 2016 (Amended: Sept 1, 2022)
Permits trial of juveniles aged 16–18 as adults for heinous crimes; 2021/2022 amendment empowered DMs for adoption orders.
Protection of Civil Rights Act (PCR)
June 1, 1955 (Renamed in 1976 from Untouchability Offences Act)
Enforces Article 17; prescribes penalties for practicing untouchability.
SC & ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
January 30, 1990 (Amended: August 20, 2018)
Prevents atrocities; Section 18A bars anticipatory bail and removes requirement of preliminary inquiry before arrest.
Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act (PESA)
December 24, 1996
Extends Part IX of Constitution to Schedule V areas, empowering traditional Gram Sabhas.
Forest Rights Act (FRA)
December 31, 2007 (Rules notified: Jan 1, 2008)
Vests individual and community forest rights in forest-dwelling STs and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers.
Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act
December 29, 2007 (State-wise notification rollout)
Legal maintenance obligation on children/heirs; empowers Maintenance Tribunals.
Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers & their Rehabilitation Act
December 6, 2013
Total ban on manual cleaning of unsanitary latrines, open drains, and sewers without protective gear.
Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act
April 19, 2017
Replaced 1995 Act; expanded disability categories from 7 to 21; provides 4% reservation in public employment and 5% in higher education.
Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act
Freezes the religious character of places of worship as they existed on August 15, 1947.
Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act
Curbs paper leaks and organized cheating in central recruitment/entrance tests; non-bailable offense.
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
July 1, 2024
Replaced IPC 1860; includes dedicated provisions on crimes against women/children, organized crime, and mob lynching.
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)
July 1, 2024
Replaced CrPC 1973; establishes digital forensics, statutory Zero FIR, and strict investigation timeframes.
